subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

The black sheep

options.text: a black dot against a white background so that it is noticed
a wolf in a black sheep's clothing
one who is not accepted as part of a family or group because of one’s bad conduct
a black sheep in a herd of white sheep, standing out from the others

solution:
The correct answer is: **one who is not accepted as part of a family or group because of one’s bad conduct**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The idiom '**The black sheep**' means a disfavored or disreputable member of a group.

 
 
• Example - *Uncle Jack, who was imprisoned for forgery, is **the black sheep**__ of the family.*
 
 

So, it is clear that the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom '**The black sheep**' is '**one who is not accepted as part of a family or group because of one’s bad conduct**'

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.
